title: Chapter 1:  UNDERSTANDING DISABILITIES AND VULNERABILITIES
content:
ሰላም ሰላም በጣም የምንወዳችሁ እና የምናከብራችሁ የEthioFresh ቤተሰቦቻችን! 👋 🎁 እንኳን ወደ Inclusiveness Chapter 1 Part 2 (የመጨረሻው ክፍል) ትምህርት በሰላም መጣችሁ! እኛ የEthioFresh ቲሞች የዩኒቨርሲቲ ቆይታችሁ ስኬታማ እንዲሆን እና በፈተና ወቅት ያለምንም ስጋት A+ እንድታስመዘግቡ በበቂ ሁኔታ የሚያዘጋጃችሁን ሙሉ ኖት ይዘንላችሁ መጥተናል። 📌 በዚህ ሁለተኛው ክፍል ቆይታችን የምንዳስሳቸው ዋና ዋና ርዕሶች PART 1 (TYPE OF DISABILITIES) ላይ የተረፉትን ይሆናል፦ * 7. Intellectual Disability: Core Criteria, Adaptive Skill Areas, Impact on Cognition/Learning/Motivation, and Levels of Support * 8. Physical Disability / Orthopedic Impairment & Health Impairment: Severity Classifications, Neurological vs. Musculoskeletal Systems, Specific Conditions, and Health Impairment Types * 9. Vulnerability: Dimensions, Causes, Characteristics, and Specific Vulnerable Groups (including Gifted and Talentedness) እናያለን! አብራችሁኝ ሁኑ👇👇👇 --- 7. INTELLECTUAL DISABILITY Core Criteria Intellectual disability is a disability characterized by significant limitations in both intellectual functioning and in adaptive behavior, which covers many everyday social and practical skills. This disability originates before the age of 18. An individual is considered to have an intellectual disability based on the following three criteria: 1. Sub average intellectual functioning: It refers to general mental capacity, such as learning, reasoning, problem solving, and so on. One way to measure intellectual functioning is an IQ test. Generally, an IQ test score of around 70 or as high as 75 indicates a limitation in intellectual functioning. 2. Significant limitations exist in two or more adaptive skill areas: It is the collection of conceptual, social, and practical skills that are learned and performed by people in their everyday lives. - Conceptual skills: language and literacy; money, time, and number concepts; and self-direction. - Social skills: interpersonal skills, social responsibility, self-esteem, gullibility, innocence (i.e., suspicion), social problem solving, and the ability to follow rules/obey laws and to avoid being victimized. - Practical skills: activities of daily living (personal care), occupational skills, healthcare, travel/transportation, schedules/routines, safety, use of money, use of the telephone. 3. Age of Onset: The condition originates before the age of 18. 💡 Intellectual Disability (የአእምሮ እድገት ውሱንነት) ማለት በአእምሮ የማሰብ/የመረዳት አቅም (Intellectual Functioning) እና በዕለታዊ የህይወት ክህሎት (Adaptive Behavior) ላይ የሚታይ ጉልህ ውሱንነት ሲሆን ከ18 ዓመት እድሜ በፊት የሚከሰት ነው። 3 መስፈርቶች አሉት፦ 1) Low IQ (ከ70-75 በታች)፣ 2) Adaptive Skill Limitation (በConceptual-ቋንቋ/ቁጥር፣ Social-የሰው ግንኙነት/ህግ ማክበር፣ እና Practical-የግል እንክብካቤ/ስልክ/ገንዘብ አጠቃቀም ላይ ውሱንነት)፣ እና 3) ከ18 ዓመት በፊት መከሰት። How Intellectual Disability Affects Academic Learning & Adaptation * General Cognition: People with intellectual disabilities vary physically and emotionally, as well as by personality, disposition, and beliefs. Their apparent slowness in learning may be related to the delayed rate of intellectual development. * Learning and Memory: The learning and memory capabilities of people with intellectual disabilities are significantly below average in comparison to peers without disabilities. Children with intellectual disabilities may not spontaneously use appropriate learning or memory retention strategies and may have difficulty in realizing the conditions or actions that aid learning and memory. However, these strategies can be taught. * Attention: To acquire information, children must attend to the learning task for the required length of time and control distractions. Children with intellectual disabilities may have difficulty distinguishing and attending to relevant questions in both learning and social situations. The problem is not that the student will not pay attention, but rather that the student does not understand or does not filter the information to get to the salient features. * Adaptive Skills: The adaptive skills of people with intellectual disabilities are often not comparable to those of their peers without disabilities. A child with intellectual disabilities may have difficulty in both learning and applying skills for a number of reasons, including a higher level of distractibility, inattentiveness, failure to read social cues, and impulsive behavior. * Speech and Language: People with intellectual disabilities may have delayed speech, language comprehension and formulation difficulties. Language problems are generally associated with delays in language development rather than with a bizarre use of language. * Motivation: People with intellectual disabilities are often described as lacking motivation, or outer-directed behavior. Past experiences of failure and the anxiety generated by those failures may make them appear to be fewer goals directed and lacking in motivation. The result of failure is often learned helplessness. The history of failure is likely to lead to dependence on external sources of reinforcement or reward rather than on internal sources of reward. * Academic Achievement: The cognitive difficulties of children with mild to moderate intellectual disabilities lead to persistent problems in academic achievement, unless intensive and extensive supports are provided. * Physical Characteristics: Children with intellectual disabilities with differing biological etiologies, may exhibit coexisting problems, such as physical, motor, orthopedic, visual and auditory impairments, and health problems. 💡 እነዚህ ተማሪዎች በትምህርታቸው ላይ የሚገጥሟቸው ዋና ችግሮች፦ ትኩረት አለመጠበቅ ሳይሆን ዋናውን መረጃ መለየት አለመቻል (Filtering issue)፣ እና በተደጋጋሚ በመውደቃቸው ምክንያት የሚፈጠር Learned Helplessness (አልችልም ብሎ ተስፋ መቁረጥና በሰው ድጋፍ ላይ ብቻ መደገፍ) ናቸው። 😅 EthioFresh Humor Break: ፈተና ሲደርስ "ኧረ አልችልበትም ተስፋ ቆርጫለሁ" ብላችሁ በሰው ኖት ላይ ብቻ ከተደገፋችሁ Learned Helplessness ይዟችኋል ማለት ነው! ተስፋ አትቁረጡ የEthioFresh ኖት ከጎናችሁ አለ! 😂 Levels of Support for Individuals with Intellectual Disabilities Levels of support range from intermittent (just occasional or “as needed” for specific activities) to pervasive (continuous in all realms of living). * 1. Intermittent Support - Duration: Only as needed. - Frequency: Occasional or infrequent. * 2. Limited Support - Duration: As needed, but sometimes continuing. - Frequency: Regular, but frequency varies. * 3. Extensive Support - Duration: Usually continuing. - Frequency: Regular, but frequency varies. * 4. Pervasive Support - Duration: May be lifelong. - Frequency: Frequent or continuous. 💡 ድጋፋቸውም ከIntermittent (አልፎ አልፎ/እንደ አስፈላጊነቱ) እስከ Pervasive (ዕድሜ ልክ ሙሉ ድጋፍ) ይደርሳል።
💡 Exam Hint: Exam questions love testing: 1) The IQ score range (70 to 75 or below), 2) The age boundary (before 18 years), 3) The 3 adaptive skills (Conceptual, Social, Practical), and 4) Matching the Levels of Support (Intermittent, Limited, Extensive, Pervasive)!
--- 8. PHYSICAL DISABILITY / ORTHOPEDIC IMPAIRMENT AND HEALTH IMPAIRMENT * Physical Disability: Physical disability is a condition that interferes with the individual’s ability to use his or her body. Many but not all, physical disabilities are orthopedic impairments. * Orthopedic Impairment: The term orthopedic impairment generally refers to conditions of muscular or skeletal system and sometimes to physical disabling conditions of the nervous system. * Health Impairment: Health impairment is a condition that requires ongoing medical attention. It includes asthma, heart defects, cancer, diabetes, hemophilia, HIV/AIDS, etc. Classification Based on Mobility and Motor Skills * A. Mild physical disability: these individuals are able to walk without aids and may make normal developmental progress. * B. Moderate physical disability: individuals can walk with braces and crutches and may have difficulty with fine-motor skills and speech production. * C. Severe physical disability: these are individuals who are wheel-chair dependent and may need special help to achieve regular development. Broad Classification of Physical Disability I. Neurological system (the brain, spinal cord & nerve) related problems With a neurological condition like cerebral palsy or a traumatic brain injury, the brain either sends the wrong instructions or interprets feedback incorrectly. * Cerebral palsy: Additional problems that can be associated include learning disabilities, mental retardation, Seizures, etc. Approximately 40 percent of those with cerebral palsy have normal intelligence. * Epilepsy: is disorder that occurs when the brain cells are not working properly and is often called a seizure disorder. Affects 1 to 2 percent of the population. Most individuals with epilepsy have normal intelligence. * Spinal bifida and spinal cord injury: damage to the spinal cord leads to paralysis and loss of sensation. The spinal bifida is a birth defect of the backbone. It usually occurs in the first twenty-six days of pregnancy. 💡 Neurological System (የነርቭና የአእምሮ): - Cerebral Palsy (40% የሚሆኑት Normal IQ አላቸው)፣ - Epilepsy (የአእምሮ ኤሌክትሪክ መዛባት፣ 1-2% ህዝብ ላይ የሚከሰት፣ አብዛኛዎቹ Normal IQ አላቸው)፣ እና - Spina Bifida (በእርግዝና በመጀመሪያዎቹ 26 ቀናት የሚከሰት የጀርባ አጥንት ጉድለት)። II. Musculoskeletal system (the muscles, bones and joints) * A. Muscular dystrophy: is an inherited condition accruing mainly in males, in which the muscles weaken and deteriorate. The weakness usually appears around 3 to 4 years of age. By age 11 most victims can no longer walk. Death usually comes between the ages of 25 and 35. * B. Arthritis: is an inflammation of the joints. * C. Amputation: a small number of children have missing limbs because of congenital abnormalities or injuiry or disease. * D. Marfan syndrome: is a genetic disorder in which the muscles are poorly developed and the spine is curved. The greatest danger is damage to aorta, which can lead to heart failure. * E. Achondroplasia: is a genetic disorder. Children with this disorder usually develop a normal torso but have a straight upper back and a curved lower back (sway back). These children are at risk of sudden death during sleep from compression of the spinal cord interfering with their breathing. * F. Polio: is viral disease that invade the brain and cause severe paralysis of the total body system. * G. Club foot: is a major orthopedic problem. This term is used to describe various ankle or foot deformities, i.e Twisting inward (equino varus) and Sharply angled at the heel (calcanel vaigus). * H. Cleft lip and cleft palate: are openings in the lip or roof of the mouth that fail to close before birth. 💡 Musculoskeletal System (የአጥንትና ጡንቻ): - Muscular Dystrophy (ወንዶች ላይ ብቻ የሚበዛ፣ ከ11 ዓመት በኋላ መራመድ የሚያቅት፣ ከ25-35 እድሜ ህይወት ሊያልፍ የሚችል)፣ - Marfan Syndrome (የልብ Aorta የመፈንዳት አደጋ ያለው)፣ - Achondroplasia (Sway back ያለው፣ በእንቅልፍ ወቅት የመታፈን አደጋ ያለው)፣ - Club foot (የእግር መጣመም - Equino varus እና Calcaneal valgus) ናቸው። Detailed List of Health Impairments 1. Heart disease: caused by improper circulation of blood by the heart. 2. Cystic fibrosis: is a hereditary disease that affects the lungs and pancreas. It leads to recurrent respiratory and digestive problems. The disease is so progressive and few who have it survive beyond age 20. 3. AIDS: caused by human immunodeficiency virus (HIV). 4. Hemophilia: is a hereditary disease in which the blood clots very slowly. The disorder is transmitted by sex-linked recessive gene and nearly always occurs in males. 5. Asthma: is a chronic respiratory condition. 6. Diabetes: inadequate secretion or use of insulin. 7. Nephrosis & Nephritis: Kidney disorders. 8. Sickle-cell anemia: Hereditary and chronic blood disease characterized by red blood cells that are distored. 9. Leukemia: excessive production of white blood Cells. 10. Lead poisoning: caused by ingesting lead-based paint chips. 11. Rheumatic fever: painful swelling and inflammation of the joints. 12. Tuberculosis: Infectious disease that commonly affects the lungs. 13. Cancer: Abnormal growth of cells. 💡 Health Impairments: ደግሞ Cystic Fibrosis (በሳንባና ቆሽት ላይ Thick mucus የሚፈጥር፣ እድሜ ከ20 አይሻገርም)፣ Hemophilia (የደም አለመርጋት - Sex-linked recessive በወንዶች ላይ የሚከሰት)፣ Sickle-Cell Anemia እና ሌሎች ከላይ የተዘረዘሩትን ያጠቃልላል።
💡 Exam Hint: High-frequency exam questions: 1) % of Cerebral Palsy with normal intelligence = 40%, 2) Spina bifida occurs in the first 26 days of pregnancy, 3) Muscular Dystrophy & Hemophilia occur mainly in males, 4) Cystic Fibrosis affects lungs & pancreas (lifespan < 20 years), 5) Marfan syndrome main danger = Aorta damage!
--- 9. VULNERABILITY Dimensions Vulnerable means being at risk of being harmed. Everyone can be harmed, so being vulnerable is part of being human. Vulnerability can be generally defined as a complex phenomenon that refers to the following dimensions: 1. Economic difficulties/lack of financial resources: poverty, low living standards. 2. Social exclusion: limited access to facilities such as transporatation, schools. 3. Lack of social support from social networks: no assistance from family members or friends. 4. Stigmatization: being a victim of stereotypes, being devalued. 5. Health difficulties: disadvantages resulting from poor mental health, physical health or disabilities. 6. Being a victim of crime: in family context especially of violence. 💡 Vulnerability (ተጋላጭነት) ማለት ለአደጋ ወይም ለጉዳት የተጋለጠ መሆን ማለት ሲሆን በ6 የህይወት ዘርፎች (Economic, Social, Health ወዘተ) ይገለጻል። Causes of Vulnerability Vulnerability may be causes by rapid population growth, poverty and hunger, poor health, low levels of education, gender inequality, and lack of access to resources and services. Environmental vulnerability concerns land degradation, earthquake, flood, hurricane, drought, storms (Monsoon rain, El Niño). 💡 መነሻ ምክንያቶቹም፦ የህዝብ ብዛት፣ ድህነት፣ የፖለቲካ ውክልና ማጣት፣ እና የተፈጥሮ አደጋዎች (ድርቅ፣ ኤልኒኞ፣ ጎርፍ) ናቸው። Characteristics of Vulnerable People 1. Less physically or mentally capable. 2. Fewer material and/or financial resources. 3. Less knowledge or experience. 4. Restricted by society to grow and develop according to their needs and potentials. Specific Groups of Vulnerable People * A. Women: particularly women in developing nations and those who are living in rural areas. * B. Children: Children are vulnerable for psychological and physical abuse (street children, orphans, etc.). * C. Minorities: ethnic or religious minority. These people are political and socially discriminated. * D. Poverty: People are vulnerable for many undesirable phenomena due to poverty. * E. Disabilities: People with disabilities very much vulnerable for abuses, poverty, illiteracy. * F. Age: Old people or very young children. * G. Illiteracy and less education: People with high rates of illiteracy and lack quality educational opportunities. * H. Sickness: Uncured health problems for example people living with HIV/AIDS. * I. Gifted and Talentedness: Gifted and talented children are vulnerable for socio-emotional developments. Due to lack of psychological support they may feel isolation as they are pulled from their regular classrooms and given instruction in separate settings and due to myths and expectations of themselves and the public. 💡 ዋና ዋና ተጋላጭ ቡድኖች፦ ሴቶች፣ ህፃናት፣ አነስተኛ ቁጥር ያላቸው ብሔረሰቦች (Minorities)፣ ድሆች፣ የአካል ጉዳተኞች፣ አረጋውያን፣ ያልተማሩ ሰዎች፣ ህመምተኞች እና Gifted and Talented (በጣም የበለፀገ አእምሮ ያላቸው ህፃናት) ናቸው። በተለይ Gifted and Talented children ለምን Vulnerable ይሆናሉ ከተባለ፦ ከተራው ክፍል ተለይተው ስለሚማሩ የመገለል ስሜት (Isolation) ስለሚሰማቸው እና ማህበረሰቡ ከእነሱ የሚጠብቀው ከፍተኛ ጫና (High expectations/myths) ስነ-ልቦናቸውን ስለሚጎዳው ነው!
💡 Exam Hint: Exam shocker alert! Teachers love asking: "Are Gifted and Talented children considered vulnerable?" The answer is YES! They are socio-emotionally vulnerable due to isolation and societal pressure!
